description: SRE + observability decomposed. SLI selection, SLO budget math, alerting (multi-window multi-burn-rate), on-call practices, postmortems, toil reduction, RED + USE methods, golden signals. Google's SRE book operationalised.

sub_mechanisms.name: SLI_selection
sub_mechanisms.definition: Pick measurements: latency p99, error rate, throughput. Tied to user experience.
sub_mechanisms.why: What you measure becomes what you optimise. Bad SLI = wrong optimisation. Good: 'request error rate seen by users'. Bad: 'CPU usage'.

sub_mechanisms.name: SLO_budget_calculation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Error budget = (1 - SLO) × time window. 99.9% / 30d = 43.2 min budget.
sub_mechanisms.why: Quantifies allowable unreliability. Spent = freeze risky changes. Unused = ship faster. Operational metric.

sub_mechanisms.name: multi_burn_rate_alerts
sub_mechanisms.definition: Alert on multiple rates: 14.4x for 1h (fast burn = critical), 6x for 6h (slow burn = page during day).
sub_mechanisms.why: Single alert: too sensitive or too slow. Multi-window: fast for catastrophic, slow for trending. Google SRE workbook standard.

sub_mechanisms.name: RED_method
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-service: Rate (requests/sec), Errors (% failed), Duration (latency distribution).
sub_mechanisms.why: Tom Wilkie framework. Three numbers tell you service health. Standard dashboard. Combined with USE for full picture.

sub_mechanisms.name: USE_method
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-resource: Utilization (% busy), Saturation (queue depth), Errors (count).
sub_mechanisms.why: Brendan Gregg. Resource-centric (CPU, disk, network). Complementary to RED. Standard for systems performance.

sub_mechanisms.name: four_golden_signals
sub_mechanisms.definition: Latency, traffic, errors, saturation. Google SRE book.
sub_mechanisms.why: Subset of RED + USE. If you monitor only four, these. Foundational dashboard.

sub_mechanisms.name: toil_definition
sub_mechanisms.definition: Manual repetitive work without lasting value. SRE goal: < 50% time on toil.
sub_mechanisms.why: Toil grows with scale linearly; engineering eliminates. Automate toil → reclaim engineering time for system improvements. Google SRE principle.

sub_mechanisms.name: blameless_postmortem_process
sub_mechanisms.definition: Document timeline, contributing factors, impact, action items. Focus on systems not individuals.
sub_mechanisms.why: Fear of blame = hidden info = no learning. Blameless = honesty = systemic fixes. Etsy + Google popularised. Standard mature practice.

sub_mechanisms.name: incident_response_roles
sub_mechanisms.definition: Incident commander, comms lead, ops lead. Clear roles during incident.
sub_mechanisms.why: Chaos during incidents counterproductive. Structure helps. ICS (Incident Command System) inspired. Standard at scale.

sub_mechanisms.name: production_readiness_review
sub_mechanisms.definition: Checklist before launching service: SLOs, monitoring, runbooks, capacity, rollback.
sub_mechanisms.why: Prevent launching with hidden issues. Standard pre-launch process. Modified for each org's needs.

sub_mechanisms.name: chaos_engineering_principles
sub_mechanisms.definition: Define steady-state hypothesis. Vary real-world events. Run in production. Minimise blast radius.
sub_mechanisms.why: Netflix Chaos Monkey + Principles of Chaos. Discipline beyond just 'break things'. Real production failures discovered + fixed before customer-visible.

sub_mechanisms.name: runbook_automation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Documented response procedures, increasingly automated. From wiki page → script → automated remediation.
sub_mechanisms.why: Common incidents auto-resolved before paging humans. PagerDuty, Rundeck, Ansible integration. Reduces MTTR + on-call burden.

derivation_rules.name: user_visible_SLIs_beat_internal_metrics
then: it's a better target than internal metrics
derivation_rules.why: CPU at 100% may be fine (work getting done). Errors seen by users → directly UX. Pick SLIs that align with user happiness. Tempting trap: easy-to-measure internal metrics not tied to UX.

derivation_rules.name: error_budget_aligns_dev_SRE_incentives
if: dev + SRE share an error budget
then: both teams have aligned incentive on reliability
derivation_rules.why: Without: dev wants to ship (risk); SRE wants stability (block). With shared budget: budget exhausted = both team's problem. Reframes conflict as shared metric. Google SRE foundation.

derivation_rules.name: multi_burn_rate_balances_sensitivity_speed
if: a single burn rate alert is used
then: it's too sensitive or too slow
derivation_rules.why: 1x burn = alert on any burn = noise. 100x burn = catastrophic-only = miss slow degradation. Multi-rate: 14.4x for 1h (page urgently), 6x for 6h (page during business hours). Operationally proven.

derivation_rules.name: blameless_postmortem_yields_better_lessons
then: systemic issues surface that blame-focused analysis misses
derivation_rules.why: Blame: people hide info, claim individual error. Blameless: 'how did system let this happen?' surfaces real causes (missing checks, unclear procedures, alert noise). Yields better fixes.

derivation_rules.name: toil_reduction_compounds_engineering_capacity
then: freed time goes to more system improvements
derivation_rules.why: Toil grows linearly with scale; manual ops = engineering time disappearing. Automation = bounded recurring cost = engineering free for improvements that further reduce toil. Compounds.
